entries.appliesTo: any person who knowingly discloses, or threatens to disclose, explicit synthetic media of an identifiable person

sources.prohibition: § 2, 18-6606(1) — 'A person is guilty of disclosing explicit synthetic media when the person knowingly: (a) Discloses explicit synthetic media and knows or reasonably should know that: (i) An identifiable person portrayed in whole or in part in the explicit synthetic media did not consent to such disclosure'
sources.coveredSubjects: § 2, 18-6606(4)(c) — '"Identifiable individual" means a person who is portrayed in whole or in part in synthetic media and who is recognizable by the person's face, likeness, or other distinguishing characteristic'
sources.penaltyMax: § 2, 18-6606(3) — 'a fine of no more than twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000)'
sources.penaltyUnit: § 2, 18-6606(2) — 'A person who violates subsection (1) of this section is guilty of a misdemeanor unless such person is guilty of a felony as provided in subsection (3) of this section'

flags: Tiered criminal structure: base offense is a misdemeanor (18-6606(2), no fine amount stated); felony 'punishable by imprisonment for a period no more than ten (10) years' when the identifiable person is under eighteen (18) years of age or on a repeat violation within the past five (5) years (18-6606(3)) — penaltyMax reflects the felony fine per rule 11
Section 1 amends the video voyeurism statute (18-6605) to add 'or threatens or conspires to disseminate, publish or sell' — not AI-specific; same criminal family, no separate segment coded
Coverage enhancement rather than restriction: base offense covers all identifiable persons; minor victims trigger the felony tier — coveredSubjects 'all-persons' is the closest single enum

Platform safe harbor: 18-6606(6) — section 'shall not apply to an interactive computer service, as defined in 47 U.S.C. 230(f)(2)... for content provided by another person, unless the provider intentionally aids or abets disclosing explicit synthetic media'
Definition of 'synthetic media' (18-6606(4)(g)) covers images/videos 'created or altered using technical means, such as artificial intelligence' — reaches non-AI technical alteration too
